title: Multi-Feature Shadow Discrimination and Adaptive Illumination Suppression for Shadow-Aware Pothole Detection
content: Apart from other vital elements of intelligent transportation and road-condition monitoring systems, vision-based pothole detection is an important one which is sensitive to the variations in illumination, especially the shadows cast by trees, buildings and vehicles. Shadows cast on the road create dark features that look like potholes, and shadows cast on top of true potholes can mask and conceal the boundaries and surface detail of the pothole, resulting in false potholes, missed potholes and less overall accuracy. In order to solve these problems, this paper puts forward a Pothole Detection Framework (SAPDF) based on the shadow awareness technology. The approach adopted is to first construct a Shadow Probability Map based on intensity, chromaticity, local contrast, texture, and edge features and then use a second stage called Shadow Pothole Discrimination to separate out illumination-induced dark regions from genuine pavement depressions. Shadows are then suppressed through an Adaptive Illumination-Guided Shadow Suppression (AIGSS) method, and the enhanced images are subsequently inputted to YOLOv11 for detection of potholes, preserving the boundaries of the potholes and the local texture. The framework is tested based on the overall detection metrics, as well as the subsets of "shadow severity". An ablation study is performed to determine the contribution of "shadow detection", "shadow discrimination", "adaptive suppression", and "structural preservation". The study will demonstrate that the explicit shadow modelling approach results in higher detection robustness under shadow-affected conditions, while preserving the detection of potholes captured under normal lighting conditions without unnecessarily changing the information, which will be the basis for reliable road-condition monitoring in complex outdoor lighting conditions.
